results.title: Niger has revised multiple resource deals since its 2023 coup.
results.description: Niger has revised multiple resource deals since its 2023 coup. It nationalized Orano’s Somaïr uranium mine in 2025, revoked Imouraren and Arlit concessions, and canceled three gold mining contracts in March 2026 for non-compliance, prompting ICSID cases. Moody’s rates it Caa3 (stable), signaling high default risk after post-coup arrears.

results.title: France’s SSA trade is ~€24B/year (<2% of total).
results.description: France’s SSA trade is ~€24B/year (<2% of total). Nuclear supplies 68% of electricity; Niger provided 15-25% of uranium historically (still ~25% of 2024 $975M imports by value) but Orano lost control post-AES. AES formed 16 Sep 2023 by Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger; expelled French forces and seized mines. France faces 0.4% 2026 growth, debt ~119% GDP and Oct 2026 protests (550k, riots). AES cut strategic access and influence, compounding energy and fiscal strains.

results.title: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger ended French military ties between 2022-2023.
results.description: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger ended French military ties between 2022-2023. Mali completed the exit in Aug 2022, Burkina Faso in Feb 2023, Niger in Dec 2023. AES formed Sept 2023. Resource control tightened later, with Niger seizing operational control of French uranium firm Orano assets in 2024-2025. Influence over minerals has decreased but full export blocks were not immediate in 2023.

results.title: The rejection of French forces in the Sahel has had limited direct impact on France's overall economy.
results.description: The rejection of French forces in the Sahel has had limited direct impact on France's overall economy. Africa is under 2% of French trade, with market share falling for decades due to competition. Niger uranium (historically 15-25% of imports) stopped after 2023-25 nationalizations; France diversified supplies from Kazakhstan, Canada and others, with no nuclear plant shortages. Orano lost operations and faced disputed stocks worth hundreds of millions of euros. Military redeployment cost hundreds of millions. Sahel economies remain small relative to France's GDP.
